newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Maize eases, wheat mixed in slow Budapest market.
newsitem.headline: Maize eases, wheat mixed in slow Budapest market.

text.p: Grain futures trade remained trendless on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Thursday as the market awaited new information to give direction, dealers said.
"We are looking at Chicago for guidance as there is little new domestic information," said Gabor Gyori of Order.
He added nearby maturities in both maize and milling wheat fell due to position-closing. May maize eased to 18,500 forints per tonne, down 10, July closed at 17,500, down 200.

Excess stocks of some 600,000 to 700,000 tonnes continued to weigh on maize prices and the Agricultural Regulatory Office said earlier today it did not plan to issue further export licences despite the fact that the latest batch of licences for 200,000 tonnes was exhausted.
Nearby milling wheat prices dropped but rose slightly for deferred contracts. Actual trade was concentrated on August.
May milling wheat lost 300 forints to end at 25,000, August closed at 21,850, down 110 and September eased 20 forints to 22,090.
Feed barley prices moved roughly in line with milling wheat but Gyori said despite today's price movements barley was confined to a narrow range of 18,000 to 19,000 forints.
Tradeless sunflowerseed rose to 42,800 forints for October, up 700, and to 43,000 forints for November, up 400, on lack of sellers.
Total grains turnover dropped to a meagre 234.6 million forints or 565 contracts compared with Wednesday's 359 million forints.
Milling wheat accounted for the bulk of turnover with 419 contracts.
